rules.accepted_credit_types: AMA PRA Category 1 Credit; CCME/AOA/AMA/ACCME/AAFP/AACOM/AAPS Category 1-A and 1-B; NMMS-certified New Mexico specific CME (max 40); postgraduate training (max 75), advanced degrees, teaching (max 40), preceptors (max 30), papers (max 30), ACLS/PALS/ATLS/NALS/ALSO, expert review (max 10)
rules.alternatives: Also accepted: ABMS board CME certificates, certification or recertification by an ABMS or osteopathic specialty board during the cycle, active AOA membership, passing COMVEX or SPEX during the cycle. Physicians practicing/residing outside the US are excused for the period of absence (notify the board).
rules.audit_note: Attest at renewal; the board audits selected renewals and may audit anytime. Keep CME records one year after the cycle in which earned. Missing documentation: possible reprimand and $500 fine. Emergency deferral up to 90 days if requested by July 1.

topics.who: Pain management CME (16.10.14.11 NMAC); counts toward the 75 hours
Review of the New Mexico Medical Practice Act and board rules, certified at triennial renewal

rules.notes: The Medical Board licenses MDs and DOs. Triennial renewal due July 1 of the renewal year (CME period July 1-June 30). From July 1, 2026 one CME hour in nutrition is required (no topic code). CME not required for telemedicine, training, public service and similar licenses.
rules.legal_basis: 16.10.4 NMAC (Continuing Medical Education); 16.10.7.9 NMAC (renewal); Medical Practice Act §61-6-21 NMSA 1978
